stem: Which screening test is specifically recommended for detecting Celiac disease in children who are known to have an $\text{IgA}$ deficiency?
explanation: Since standard Celiac screens rely on $\text{IgA}$, an $\text{IgG}$-based test like the deamidated antigliadin antibody is necessary for accurate screening in $\text{IgA}$-deficient patients.
rationale: Standard screening involves $\text{IgA}$ antibodies, so a patient lacking $\text{IgA}$ would require a test based on a different immunoglobulin class.

optionExplanations.A: Since standard Celiac screens rely on $\text{IgA}$, an $\text{IgG}$-based test like the deamidated antigliadin antibody is necessary for accurate screening in $\text{IgA}$-deficient patients.
optionExplanations.B: This is the standard screen for the general population, but it will yield a false negative in children who cannot produce $\text{IgA}$.
optionExplanations.C: The source material notes that the combined antigliadin $\text{IgA}$ and $\text{IgG}$ test is no longer recommended or reliable.
optionExplanations.D: While highly specific, this is an $\text{IgA}$-based test and would be ineffective in a patient with an $\text{IgA}$ deficiency.
